couplets.gloss: Seek out people who have spent a long life doing right, treat them with respect, and work at winning their friendship.

edges.reason: Urges winning the friendship of those whom long right living has matured.
edges.quote: the friendship of the wise

edges.reason: Its subject is the elder seasoned by years of doing right.
edges.quote: who know righteousness and have grown old in it

edges.reason: Points anyone seeking a guide towards those long practised in right living.
edges.quote: choose with care the friendship of the wise

couplets.gloss: Make a real effort to stay close to people who can get you out of the trouble you're in and keep the next trouble away.

edges.reason: Prizes as friends those who can mend today's trouble and head off tomorrow's.
edges.quote: cultivate thou their friendship with ardour

couplets.gloss: Few things are harder to come by than having truly great people care about you and treat you as one of their own.

edges.reason: Ranks making the great your own as the rarest thing of all.
edges.quote: to cherish the great and make them your own

edges.reason: Concerns the great themselves, and how rare it is to make them your own.
edges.quote: cherish the great

couplets.gloss: Having people better than you as your close companions gives you more strength than anything else could.

edges.reason: Holds that closeness with one's betters outmatches every other kind of strength.
edges.quote: the highest of all strengths

edges.reason: Speaks of people who stand above oneself in worth.
edges.quote: those greater than you

couplets.gloss: A ruler sees his realm through his advisers, so he must look hard at them before he picks them.

edges.reason: Tells the ruler himself to take care in picking his councillors.
edges.quote: he should choose them with care

edges.reason: Says what his advisers are to a ruler: the eyes he goes forward with.
edges.quote: his advisers as his eyes

edges.reason: A ruler goes forward with his advisers serving as his eyes.
edges.quote: his advisers as his eyes

edges.reason: Since a ruler goes by his advisers, they must be weighed before being taken on.
edges.quote: choose them with care

couplets.gloss: Someone who can live as one of a circle of good people has nothing to fear from those who wish them harm.

edges.reason: Standing among the worthy leaves one's enemies with nothing they can do.
edges.quote: keep worthy company

couplets.gloss: Nobody can bring you down if you keep friends who will tell you to your face when you're wrong.

edges.reason: Puts beyond ruin anyone who keeps companions able to rebuke them.
edges.quote: companions who will rebuke you

edges.reason: For anyone stung by criticism: such critics are what keeps a person from ruin.
edges.quote: who has the power to ruin you

couplets.gloss: A ruler with nobody around to challenge him will fall without any enemy having to lift a finger.

edges.reason: Shows the price of having no one to rebuke him: ruin with no enemy in sight.
edges.quote: will fall even with no one to bring him down

edges.reason: Turns the point on the ruler who lets himself go unchallenged.
edges.quote: A ruler with no one to rebuke him

couplets.gloss: You can't make a profit without capital, and you can't stay steady in life without wise people to lean on.

edges.reason: As trade needs capital, standing firm needs someone to lean on.
edges.quote: a prop to lean on

couplets.gloss: Making lots of enemies is stupid, but walking away from good friends does ten times more damage.

edges.reason: Counts dropping good companions as ten times worse than raising a host of foes.
edges.quote: ten times worse

couplets.gloss: Truly great people steer clear of a bad crowd, while petty people treat that same crowd as their relatives.

edges.reason: Shows the worthy shrinking from the low crowd that smaller men embrace.
edges.quote: Greatness fears petty company

edges.reason: A small nature gives itself away by feeling at home among the vulgar.
edges.quote: Pettiness treats it as kin

couplets.gloss: Just as water picks up the qualities of the ground it runs through, your mind picks up the qualities of the people around you.
keywords: you become who you hang out with

edges.reason: States how company works: it changes understanding as the ground changes water.
edges.quote: People’s understanding takes on the nature of their company

edges.reason: Warns someone in a bad circle that their understanding will take on its nature.
edges.quote: takes on the nature of their company

couplets.gloss: What you perceive comes from your own mind, but what people call you comes from who you are seen with.

edges.reason: Says a man's name in the world is settled by the people he keeps.
edges.quote: What people call them comes from their company

couplets.gloss: Your character looks like it comes from within, but it really sits with the people you spend your time with.

edges.reason: Moves a person’s understanding out of the mind and into the company they keep.
edges.quote: it lies in their company

couplets.gloss: Having a clean mind and doing clean deeds both come from keeping clean company.

edges.reason: Makes clean company the ground on which clean thought and clean deeds both stand.
edges.quote: both depend on pure company

couplets.gloss: People with a clean mind leave a good line behind them, and those who keep good company find that nothing they do goes wrong.

edges.reason: Promises that what the pure of mind leave behind will be good.
edges.quote: What the pure of mind leave behind is good

edges.reason: Says every undertaking goes well for those among good people.
edges.quote: no deed fails to turn out well

couplets.gloss: A good heart is what really enriches a person, and being among good people brings every kind of honour.

edges.reason: Credits goodness of mind with the prosperity it brings.
edges.quote: A good mind brings living beings prosperity

edges.reason: Credits all of a man's honour to the virtuous people around him.
edges.quote: Good company brings every kind of glory

edges.reason: Uses the word treasure for a state of heart, not for goods.
edges.quote: a treasure unto a man

couplets.gloss: Even people who are already thoroughly good find that good companions make them far more secure.

edges.reason: Even the noble, whose minds are good, find protection in good company.
edges.quote: find protection in good company

couplets.gloss: Goodness earns you a place in the next world, and good friends are what keep you practising it.

edges.reason: Even the next world, which comes from a good mind, finds its protection in good company.
edges.quote: finds its protection in good company

couplets.gloss: Nothing helps you more than being around good people, and nothing hurts you more than being around bad ones.

edges.reason: Names good company the best ally a person can have.
edges.quote: no help greater than good company

edges.reason: Anyone weighing up their circle should know that no harm outdoes the wrong people.
edges.quote: nothing causes more grief than bad company

couplets.gloss: Before you start anything, work out what it will cost you, what you could lose and what you stand to gain.

edges.reason: Asks for cost, loss and gain to be reckoned before the first move.
edges.quote: Weigh what will be lost, what will be gained

edges.reason: Gives anyone planning a venture the first job: weigh loss, gain and later profit.
edges.quote: the profit it will bring later, then act

couplets.gloss: A leader who decides only after talking it through with carefully chosen advisers can achieve anything.

edges.reason: Nothing is out of reach for one who decides only after counsel with proven men.
edges.quote: examine a task with people they have chosen

edges.reason: Puts this to a ruler with councillors to draw on.
edges.quote: Behold the prince who decideth upon action

couplets.gloss: Sensible people stay away from ventures that dangle big returns but could wipe out everything you put in.

edges.reason: The wise look past the promised gain to what the venture could cost them.
edges.quote: The wise won’t start a venture

edges.reason: Warns off any venture that tempts with profit and risks the capital itself.
edges.quote: looks for profit and loses the capital

couplets.gloss: People who don't want to look foolish never begin a thing until they're clear about it.

edges.reason: Dread of ridicule keeps such men from starting anything they have not thought out.
edges.quote: won’t begin what they are not sure of

couplets.gloss: Going to war without a full plan just hands your enemy a well-prepared place to grow strong.

edges.reason: Demands that every detail be planned before one marches, or the enemy profits.
edges.quote: without thinking through every side of it

edges.reason: Shows what a war begun without planning costs: it strengthens the foe.
edges.quote: planting your enemies

edges.reason: Pictures the rash fighter bedding out his enemy like a seedling in ready soil.
edges.quote: planting your enemies in a prepared bed

couplets.gloss: Doing what you shouldn't will ruin you, and so will failing to do what you should.
Think before you commit: telling yourself you'll think it over once you've begun is a fool's mistake.

edges.reason: Forbids starting first and promising oneself to think it over later.
edges.quote: Think, then commit to the task

couplets.gloss: Work done the wrong way fails, however many people pitch in to save it.

edges.reason: A wrong method wastes all the labour, whatever numbers are added to the task.
edges.quote: Effort not made the right way will crack

couplets.gloss: You can get it wrong even when you mean well, if what you do for someone doesn't suit who they are.

edges.reason: Even a kindness must be thought out against the nature of the one receiving it.
edges.quote: Even doing good can go wrong

couplets.gloss: Only take on what can't be criticised, because people look down on anyone who does something beneath them.

edges.reason: The world scorns what doesn’t suit you, so choose only what no one will scorn.
edges.quote: do what no one will scorn

couplets.gloss: Before you begin, size up the job, your own power, your opponent's power and the backing each side can call on.

edges.reason: Lists what to weigh before acting: the task, oneself, the enemy, and both sets of allies.
edges.quote: Weigh the strength of the task, your own strength

couplets.gloss: A ruler who knows what he can do, learns what he needs to and stays inside that will never see a campaign fail.

edges.reason: Promises unfailing success to one who stays inside his own known force.
edges.quote: know what they can do

edges.reason: Speaks of a ruler planning campaigns against other lands.
edges.quote: his invasions will never fail

couplets.gloss: Plenty of people have got carried away, misjudged how strong they were, charged in and been destroyed halfway through.

edges.reason: Points to the many who misjudged their own force and fell midway.
edges.quote: not knowing the strength they have

couplets.gloss: Anyone who won't get along with others, doesn't know their own limits and admires themselves is soon finished.

edges.reason: Not knowing one's measure is one of three faults that bring a swift end.
edges.quote: don’t know their measure

edges.reason: Self-admiration joins the list of what ruins a man quickly.
edges.quote: admire themselves

couplets.gloss: Even something as light as peacock feathers will snap a cart's axle if you keep piling them on.

edges.reason: However light each load, a limit stands beyond which the whole thing breaks.
edges.quote: if you pile them too high

edges.reason: A cart’s axle gives way under a mass of peacock feathers.
edges.quote: a cart loaded with peacock feathers will break its axle

edges.reason: Shows someone overcommitted how many light loads, added up, can snap the axle.
edges.quote: will break its axle, if you pile them too high

couplets.gloss: Once you've reached the very tip of the branch, trying to go higher will kill you.

edges.reason: One who has reached his limit and presses on throws away his life.
edges.quote: try to go further

edges.reason: The topmost branch stands for the utmost reach of a person's strength.
edges.quote: the top of the tree

edges.reason: For one already at full stretch, the next step up is the dangerous one.
edges.quote: will lose their life

couplets.gloss: Give according to what you can actually afford: that's how you look after your money and still share it.

edges.reason: Ties the size of one's gifts to the size of one's means.
edges.quote: Give in the right way, knowing your limit

couplets.gloss: A small income is no disaster as long as what goes out stays smaller than what comes in.

edges.reason: A thin inflow does no harm while the outflow is kept from outgrowing it.
edges.quote: as long as the way out is no wider

edges.reason: Earning and spending are the channels that fill a tank and drain it.
edges.quote: the feeder channel

edges.reason: Gives the overspender the whole rule: never let more run out than runs in.
edges.quote: the way out is no wider

couplets.gloss: People who don't live within their means can seem to be doing well, then collapse and leave nothing behind.

edges.reason: A life run past one's means may pass for prosperity until it vanishes.
edges.quote: A life not lived within its limit

edges.reason: Warns the overspender that the look of prosperity is no proof of safety.
edges.quote: seems to be there

couplets.gloss: If you give freely without checking what you really have, your money runs out fast.

edges.reason: Helping others without weighing what you have soon ruins your wealth.
edges.quote: without weighing what you have

couplets.gloss: A crow can beat an owl in daylight, so a ruler who wants to win must pick his moment.

edges.reason: The crow beats the owl only by day, so a ruler must choose his hour.
edges.quote: need the right time

edges.reason: Given to the ruler who means to defeat an enemy.
edges.quote: Rulers who would beat their enemies

edges.reason: The crow beats the owl only by day: every creature has its hour, and so has a ruler.
edges.quote: By day the crow beats the owl

couplets.gloss: Moving in step with the seasons of things is the rope that keeps prosperity tied to you.

edges.reason: Keeping step with the season is the rope that holds prosperity fast.
edges.quote: Acting in step with the season

edges.reason: திரு, good fortune, is pictured as a restless thing that must be roped to stay.
edges.quote: a rope that ties good fortune down

couplets.gloss: Nothing is out of reach if you begin at the right moment and with the right tools.

edges.reason: With the right season and means, the word impossible loses its meaning.
edges.quote: if you have the means and know the time

couplets.gloss: You could win the whole world if you pick the right moment and the right place to act.

edges.reason: The right hour would put even the whole world within one's grasp.
edges.quote: an eye to the time

edges.reason: Where you act counts along with when you act.
edges.quote: the time and the place

couplets.gloss: People set on winning big wait calmly for their chance, without panicking or rushing.

edges.reason: Those who aim at the whole world stay still and watch for the time.
edges.quote: watch for the time

edges.reason: While the moment is unclear, the counsel is to stay still and keep watching, unshaken.
edges.quote: stay still, unshaken

couplets.gloss: When a driven person holds back, it's like a ram stepping backwards to gather force for the charge.

edges.reason: A pause by the energetic is only the backward step before the blow.
edges.quote: When a person of spirit holds back

edges.reason: The ram draws back before its blow, as a strong man waits before he acts.
edges.quote: a fighting ram drawing back to charge

couplets.gloss: Smart people don't let their anger show right away; they keep it inside and wait for the right time.

edges.reason: Even a grievance is held back until the moment comes to act on it.
edges.quote: watch for the time and burn within

couplets.gloss: Put up with your opponents while they're strong; when their time of weakness comes, they'll fall easily.
couplets.sensitive: counsels submitting to an adversary; could reach someone being abused

edges.reason: Bows to an adversary only until his hour of decline comes round.
edges.quote: When you see their end

couplets.gloss: When a rare opportunity comes along, don't hesitate: go straight for even the hardest thing.

edges.reason: A rare opening is to be used at once, even on the hardest task.
edges.quote: at that very moment

edges.reason: An uncommon chance is the one time not to wait.
edges.quote: When what is hard to come by comes your way

couplets.gloss: When conditions are against you, stay still like a waiting heron; when they turn, strike as fast as it does.

edges.reason: Asks for the heron’s stillness while you wait and its strike when your moment comes.
edges.quote: be like the heron

edges.reason: Gives the whole rule for one torn between acting and waiting: hold still, then strike.
edges.quote: be like its strike

edges.reason: The heron stands idle until the moment comes, then strikes at once.
edges.quote: In the time for holding still, be like the heron

couplets.gloss: Don't start a fight or any project, and don't write anyone off, until you have fully seen the ground you'd be working on.

edges.reason: Forbids any move until ground for a siege has been found.
edges.quote: until you have found the ground for a siege

couplets.gloss: Even the mightiest gain a great deal by working from a fortified base.

edges.reason: Even the strong profit by resting their power on strongholds.
edges.quote: a gain that rests on a stronghold

couplets.gloss: Even the weaker side can stand firm and beat a stronger one by picking the right ground and moving with care.

edges.reason: The right ground, used with care, lets the weak bring down the strong.
edges.quote: if they know the place

edges.reason: Tells the outmatched side to fight only where the field favours it.
edges.quote: Even the weak grow strong and win

couplets.gloss: Your opponents' plans come to nothing if you work from a strong position that you know well.

edges.reason: Ground well chosen and held close undoes whatever the other side has planned.
edges.quote: lose their plan

couplets.gloss: A crocodile rules in deep water, but out of it even its enemies can toy with it.

edges.reason: Power belongs to the ground: the crocodile's rule ends at the water's edge.
edges.quote: In deep water the crocodile beats everything

edges.reason: In deep water the crocodile rules, and out of it is a plaything: ground decides.
edges.quote: Out of the water, everything else beats it

couplets.gloss: A sturdy chariot can't run on the sea and an ocean ship can't sail on land: each works only where it belongs.

edges.reason: Chariot and ship each count for nothing once off their own element.
edges.quote: can’t run on the sea

edges.reason: The mighty chariot is useless the moment it leaves the land.
edges.quote: Tall chariots with strong wheels

edges.reason: The great ship is as helpless ashore as the chariot is afloat.
edges.quote: Ships that run on the sea can’t run on land

couplets.gloss: A leader who plans everything in advance and strikes from the right place needs nothing else but courage.

edges.reason: Once all is planned, fearlessness is the only ally still required.
edges.quote: You need no help but fearlessness

edges.reason: Acting to suit the place is part of what leaves no need for other help.
edges.quote: act to suit the place

edges.reason: Drawn for a ruler deciding how to strike.
edges.quote: Behold the prince that hath planned everything beforehand

couplets.gloss: A ruler with a small army can make a big army's efforts useless just by taking up the right ground.

edges.reason: Right ground alone can make a strong foe's efforts come to nothing.
edges.quote: reaches ground that suits it

edges.reason: Speaks to a ruler whose army is the weaker one.
edges.quote: the one with a small army

couplets.gloss: People defending their home ground are hard to beat, even with no fortifications or other advantages.

edges.reason: A people's own soil guards them even where walls and other aids are lacking.
edges.quote: it is hard to attack people on the land where they live

couplets.gloss: An elephant that stares down a line of spearmen can be killed by a jackal once it's stuck in a swamp.

edges.reason: Bad ground hands a jackal what spearmen could not take.
edges.quote: in mud where its legs sink

edges.reason: The fearless war elephant, mired in a marsh, falls to a jackal.
edges.quote: A fearless tusker

couplets.gloss: Test someone four ways before you trust them: on principle, money, pleasure and fear for their life.

edges.reason: Names the four trials a person must pass before being trusted.
edges.quote: Test someone by these four

edges.reason: Three of its four tests are the aims of life: righteousness, wealth and pleasure.
edges.quote: righteousness, wealth, pleasure

couplets.gloss: Pick someone from a decent family, free of faults, who would hate to be disgraced.

edges.reason: Sums up whom to trust by family, clean record and dread of disgrace.
edges.quote: Trust the one who is born of good family

edges.reason: Good family is the first of its three marks of the trustworthy.
edges.quote: born of good family

edges.reason: Dread of disgrace is its last mark, the shame that restrains a man.
edges.quote: the shame that dreads a scar

couplets.gloss: Look closely and you'll find that even the most learned and faultless people have gaps in what they know.
Add up someone's good points and bad points, and judge them by whichever is greater.

edges.reason: Sets the rule of judgment: a person's nature is whichever side outweighs the other.
edges.quote: see which are more, and judge them by that

couplets.gloss: If you want to know whether someone is great or petty, look at what they actually do.

edges.reason: Makes a person's own deeds the one test of greatness or pettiness.
edges.quote: their own deeds are the touchstone

edges.reason: Deeds are the stone on which a man's metal is assayed.
edges.quote: the touchstone

couplets.gloss: Be careful about trusting people with no family or ties: with nothing to hold them, they won't mind disgrace.
couplets.sensitive: treats people without family as untrustworthy

edges.reason: Warns that one with no kin has nothing to bind him and no shame to lose.
edges.quote: Do not trust those who have no one

couplets.gloss: Pick a fool as your confidant because you're fond of them, and you'll be led into one stupid mistake after another.

edges.reason: Trusting on fondness in place of a proper trial brings every kind of folly.
edges.quote: leaning on your fondness for them

couplets.gloss: Trust someone without testing them first and you make trouble that reaches even your descendants.

edges.reason: Shows the cost of skipping the trial: evils that run on to one's descendants.
edges.quote: even for those who come after you

edges.reason: Before confiding in a newcomer, give them a real trial first.
edges.quote: Trust a stranger without testing them

couplets.gloss: Don't trust anyone until you've tested them, and once you have, give each person the job that suits them.

edges.reason: Puts the trial first, and only then the matching of each person to a task.
edges.quote: Trust no one without testing them

couplets.gloss: Trusting someone untested and doubting someone already proven are equally sure ways to bring on endless trouble.

edges.reason: Adds that doubting a proven man does as much harm as trusting an unproven one.
edges.quote: to doubt someone you have come to trust

couplets.gloss: Hire the person who looks at both the good and bad of things and then goes for what is actually good.

edges.reason: Prizes the servant whose eye takes in both good and evil and settles on the good.
edges.quote: looks at both the good and the bad

edges.reason: Describes whom to take into one's service.
edges.quote: is the one to employ

couplets.gloss: Put in charge someone who can grow what you have and put right whatever goes wrong.

edges.reason: Names what an officer is for: growing resources and curing what ails them.
edges.quote: widen the sources of income

edges.reason: Speaks to one with a kingdom, telling him whom to set over it.
edges.quote: the resources of thy kingdom

couplets.gloss: Choose only someone who has warmth, intelligence and decisiveness, and who isn't greedy.

edges.reason: Sets out the four marks of one fit for service.
edges.quote: truly has these four

edges.reason: Loving-kindness is the first mark asked of an officer.
edges.quote: loving-kindness

edges.reason: Understanding is the second thing looked for in a servant.
edges.quote: understanding

edges.reason: Firmness of mind is the third requirement.
edges.quote: firmness

edges.reason: Its fourth mark is freedom from craving, the Tamil’s அவா.
edges.quote: freedom from craving

couplets.gloss: Plenty of people pass every test and then turn out differently once they actually do the job.

edges.reason: Warns that a servant who passed every trial may change once at the work.
edges.quote: many people change with the nature of the work

couplets.gloss: Give work to people for their know-how and staying power, not because they're devoted to you.

edges.reason: Judges workers by what they know and can endure, not by their devotion.
edges.quote: one who knows how and can endure to the end

edges.reason: Tells anyone hiring to weigh skill and stamina, and to set fondness aside.
edges.quote: not something to hand to a favourite

couplets.gloss: Find the right person and the right job for them, make sure the timing is right, then have them start.

edges.reason: Look closely at the doer before handing over the work.
edges.quote: Look closely at the doer

edges.reason: Even with the right worker, the work must be matched to the right time.
edges.quote: match them to the time

couplets.gloss: Work out what someone can do and which job suits them, then leave it in their hands.

edges.reason: Concerns the servant, whose capacity is to be judged before he is given charge.
edges.quote: this person can finish this task by this means

edges.reason: Gives the last step in choosing someone: having judged them, let them run it.
edges.quote: leave it in their hands

couplets.gloss: Once you've decided someone is right for a role, give them what they need to do it well.

edges.reason: Once someone is found right for a task, it must be made theirs.
edges.quote: make that task theirs

couplets.gloss: Prosperity walks away from the boss who takes a good worker's closeness the wrong way.

edges.reason: Concerns the able servant whose approaches a master misreads.
edges.quote: someone devoted to the work

edges.reason: Assures the resented worker that the loss falls on the one who resents them.
edges.quote: good fortune will leave you

edges.reason: திரு, which he reads as the goddess, walks out on such a master.
edges.quote: good fortune will leave you

couplets.gloss: A ruler should check on things every day, because a country stays straight as long as its officials stay straight.

edges.reason: Asks for a daily watch, since the realm stands or falls with its officers.
edges.quote: look into it every day

edges.reason: A standing order given to the ruler in so many words.
edges.quote: Let the ruler look into it every day

edges.reason: Makes the officers' soundness the measure of the country's.
edges.quote: If the one who does the work doesn’t go crooked, the world won’t

couplets.gloss: Only family keep up their old bond with you even when you've lost everything.

edges.reason: Makes faithfulness through hard times the mark of kin alone.
edges.quote: Only kin go on cherishing old ties

couplets.gloss: If your relatives' love for you never fades, your good fortune will keep on growing.

edges.reason: Sees gains that keep sprouting in the unending fondness of one’s kin.
edges.quote: kin whose fondness never ends

couplets.gloss: Someone who doesn't enjoy being close to their relatives is like a reservoir with no banks: what they have simply drains away.

edges.reason: Without closeness of heart, a life runs off like water with no bank to hold it.
edges.quote: no sharing of hearts

edges.reason: A tank with no banks pictures a life with no kin to hold wealth in.
edges.quote: a broad tank filling with water and no bank around it

couplets.gloss: The real point of being well off is to bring your relatives close and keep them there.

edges.reason: Names gathering one's relations as the whole purpose of prosperity.
edges.quote: live so that your kin gather round you

couplets.gloss: Speak gently and give openly, and your relatives will crowd around you.

edges.reason: Promises a man ranks of relatives drawn in by how he treats them.
edges.quote: surrounded by kin, rank upon rank

edges.reason: Credits a pleasant tongue with holding a family around one.
edges.quote: speak sweetly

edges.reason: Giving is the other half of what brings relatives near.
edges.quote: If you can give

couplets.gloss: Nobody in the world has more devoted relatives than someone who gives freely and doesn't hold on to anger.

edges.reason: Free giving wins the most devoted relatives the world can show.
edges.quote: a great giver

edges.reason: Shunning anger is the other thing that keeps relatives attached.
edges.quote: doesn’t cherish anger

edges.reason: Holds that no one on earth has kin more closely bound to him.
edges.quote: No one on this wide earth has more people at their side

couplets.gloss: A crow calls the others over instead of hiding its food; wealth stays only with people who share like that.

edges.reason: Holds up the crow that calls its fellows to eat as the pattern for those who would prosper.
edges.quote: It calls the others and eats

couplets.gloss: A ruler does well to treat relatives by their merit, not all alike, because many stay close for that recognition.

edges.reason: Graded honours, rather than one treatment for all, keep many relatives attached.
edges.quote: each by their rank

edges.reason: Advice for a ruler on how to rank his own relations.
edges.quote: If a ruler looks on people not all alike

couplets.gloss: A relative who has drifted away will come back once you deal with whatever caused the rift.

edges.reason: A cooled bond is mended by taking away its cause.
edges.quote: once the cause of the rift is gone

edges.reason: Treats the estranged relative as someone who can readily be won back.
edges.quote: will come back as kin

edges.reason: Offers a way through a family rift: find the cause, remove it, expect them back.
edges.quote: Those who were your own and left you will come back

couplets.gloss: If a relative who broke with you comes back for some reason of their own, take them in, but stay careful.

edges.reason: Keeps the door open to a relative who returns, though not blindly.
edges.quote: take them in

edges.reason: Concerns the relation who left and has returned with a motive.
edges.quote: someone who left comes back for a reason

edges.reason: Says to take back a returning relative while keeping one's eyes open.
edges.quote: think it through and take them in

couplets.gloss: Letting your guard down because you're pleased with yourself does more harm than even a terrible rage.

edges.reason: Rates carelessness born of delight as worse than the worst rage.
edges.quote: Worse than boundless rage is the carelessness

couplets.gloss: Feeling too safe destroys your good name, the way constant poverty destroys your ability to think.

edges.reason: Sets carelessness beside want: one kills glory as the other kills understanding.
edges.quote: Carelessness kills glory

couplets.sensitive: says daily poverty kills a person’s understanding; could shame someone in want

couplets.gloss: People who aren't careful never earn lasting renown, and every school of thought agrees on that.

edges.reason: Cites every school of thought for the verdict that the careless win no renown.
edges.quote: There is no glory for the careless

couplets.gloss: Forts are no use to the fearful, and being well supplied is no use to the careless.

edges.reason: Walls do nothing for one whose nerve has already gone.
edges.quote: no fort for those who are afraid

edges.reason: Nothing good stays with one who has stopped taking care.
edges.quote: there is no good for the careless

couplets.gloss: If you don't protect yourself in advance, you'll regret your carelessness when trouble catches you off guard.

edges.reason: Urges defence laid down beforehand, ahead of any surprise.
edges.quote: fails to guard in advance

edges.reason: Shows the negligent man lamenting only after disaster has struck.
edges.quote: will regret that mistake when the blow lands

couplets.gloss: Nothing compares with never letting your guard down, at any time or with anyone.

edges.reason: Nothing, it says, can compare with a guard kept up always and against everyone.
edges.quote: with everyone, at all times, without fail

couplets.gloss: There's nothing you can't do if you bring an alert, careful mind to your work.

edges.reason: A mind that never drops its guard makes every task possible.
edges.quote: the tool of unbroken attention

couplets.gloss: A ruler must stick to the work the wise approve of; neglect it and he pays through all his lives to come.

edges.reason: Neglect of what is praised leaves a person with nothing in all seven births.
edges.quote: have nothing, in all seven births

edges.reason: An order laid on the ruler by name.
edges.quote: The prince shall devote himself assiduously

couplets.gloss: When you're feeling pleased with yourself and carried away, think of the people ruined by letting their guard down.

edges.reason: Bids the elated man recall those whom carelessness destroyed.
edges.quote: those who were ruined by neglect

edges.reason: Gives a plain remedy for a swelling head: remember who fell that way.
edges.quote: When your delight makes you feel strong

couplets.gloss: Getting what you want is easy as long as you keep your goal in mind at all times.
keywords: keeping your eye on the prize

edges.reason: Whatever is wanted comes easily to one who never lets the aim slip from mind.
edges.quote: if you can keep your mind on it

couplets.gloss: Real justice means looking into the matter carefully, favouring nobody and taking advice from those who know the law.

edges.reason: Spells out what justice consists of: inquiry, no leaning, and counsel with the law.
edges.quote: that is justice

couplets.gloss: Just as all life depends on rain from the sky, people depend on their ruler's justice to protect them.

edges.reason: Makes a ruler's justice as vital to his people as rain to the world.
edges.quote: A ruler’s people live looking to his sceptre

edges.reason: Shows the people looking to their ruler for safety.
edges.quote: A ruler’s people

edges.reason: The sky everyone looks to for rain stands for a ruler everyone depends on.
edges.quote: All the world lives looking to the sky

edges.reason: The sceptre is what the people watch, as the world watches the sky.
edges.quote: looking to his sceptre

couplets.gloss: A ruler's just authority is what holds up both the scriptures of the learned and moral order itself.

edges.reason: Rests both scripture and moral order on the ruler's justice.
edges.quote: at the root of the books of the sages and of righteousness

edges.reason: Places the books of the sages under the ruler’s protection.
edges.quote: the books of the sages

edges.reason: The sceptre stands as the prop under all learning and right.
edges.quote: The ruler’s sceptre stands

couplets.gloss: A ruler who governs his people with real care will never lose his throne.

edges.reason: Caring rule is repaid by a world that clings to the ruler’s feet.
edges.quote: holds his people close and wields the sceptre

edges.reason: Holds up the good ruler and what his care wins him.
edges.quote: the great ruler

couplets.gloss: In a land ruled by law, the rains come on time and the harvests are good.

edges.reason: Rain in season and rich crops are promised to a land ruled lawfully.
edges.quote: Rain and harvest come together

edges.reason: Ties the land's fortunes to how its ruler conducts his office.
edges.quote: a ruler who wields the sceptre as it should be wielded

edges.reason: The sceptre held according to law is the sign of the good reign.
edges.quote: wields the sceptre as it should be wielded

couplets.gloss: A ruler's victories come from justice rather than weapons, as long as his justice is straight and favours no side.

edges.reason: Credits victory to straight justice and not to armed force.
edges.quote: that only if it doesn’t bend

edges.reason: Corrects a ruler's notion of what actually wins his wars.
edges.quote: brings a ruler victory

edges.reason: The unbent sceptre replaces the weapon as the true means of winning.
edges.quote: It is the sceptre

edges.reason: The spear is named only to be set below the sceptre.
edges.quote: It is not the spear

couplets.gloss: A ruler protects everyone under him, and his own even-handed justice protects him in turn.

edges.reason: The ruler guards the people, and unbending justice guards the ruler.
edges.quote: Justice guards him

edges.reason: Calls the ruler the protector of all who live under him.
edges.quote: The ruler guards the whole world

edges.reason: The sceptre takes up the ruler's own task of guarding, on condition it stays upright.
edges.quote: alloweth it not ever to lean to either side

couplets.gloss: A ruler who is hard to reach and careless in judging cases brings himself down, even with no enemies.

edges.reason: Being out of reach helps bring down a ruler who has no enemy at all.
edges.quote: isn’t easy to reach

edges.reason: Careless hearing of causes is the other half of this ruler's fall.
edges.quote: doesn’t look into things and give justice

edges.reason: A warning to the ruler who keeps his people at a distance.
edges.quote: A ruler who isn’t easy to reach

couplets.gloss: A ruler who protects his people from every threat isn't at fault when he punishes wrongdoers: that's his job.

edges.reason: Clears a protecting ruler's punishments of reproach: they are his work.
edges.quote: no stain on a ruler

edges.reason: Speaks of the ruler who guards his people from threats within and without.
edges.quote: To protect his people from others

couplets.gloss: Executing the worst criminals is like a farmer pulling weeds so the crop can grow.
couplets.sensitive: approves of putting offenders to death

edges.reason: Likens a ruler's execution of the wicked to weeding a crop.
edges.quote: pulling weeds from a green crop

edges.reason: The Tamil names the ruler as the one who punishes.
edges.quote: A ruler who punishes the wicked with death

couplets.gloss: A ruler who oppresses his people and does wrong is worse than a murderer.

edges.reason: Ranks an oppressing ruler below even those who have taken up killing.
edges.quote: crueller than those who have taken up killing

edges.reason: Turned on the ruler who wrongs those under him.
edges.quote: A ruler who takes to tormenting people

couplets.gloss: When someone in power 'asks' you for something, it's really a robber holding you up.

edges.reason: Unmasks a ruler's polite request as a robbery on the road.
edges.quote: one who stands with a spear

edges.reason: Aimed at the one who holds the office and makes the demand.
edges.quote: one who stands with a sceptre

edges.reason: The sceptre, meant for justice, is made the robber's threat.
edges.quote: stands with a sceptre

couplets.gloss: A ruler who doesn't look into things every day and put them right loses his country bit by bit.

edges.reason: Failing daily to set wrongs right wears a ruler's power away by the day.
edges.quote: doesn’t look into things daily and do justice

edges.reason: Warns the ruler who will not look into his own government.
edges.quote: When a ruler doesn’t look into things daily

couplets.gloss: A ruler who carelessly strays from justice loses his wealth and his people together.

edges.reason: A bent sceptre costs the ruler both his riches and his people.
edges.quote: bends the sceptre and acts without thinking

edges.reason: Points at the unthinking ruler, whom his own course undoes.
edges.quote: A ruler who bends the sceptre

couplets.gloss: The tears of people who can't bear their oppression are what grind down a ruler's wealth.

edges.reason: Oppression is paid for out of the ruler's own wealth, worn down by his victims' weeping.
edges.quote: the weapon that wears away wealth

edges.reason: Gives the oppressed people the last word against their ruler.
edges.quote: those who suffer and can’t bear it

edges.reason: Names the prosperity at stake as the ruler's.
edges.quote: the prosperity of the prince

edges.reason: Tears become a weapon that wears down wealth.
edges.quote: The tears wept

couplets.gloss: Fair rule is what earns rulers a lasting name, and unfair rule dims it.

edges.reason: Says what lasts for rulers comes from the straight sceptre.
edges.quote: What makes rulers last is the straight sceptre

edges.reason: Without the straight sceptre a ruler’s light won’t last.
edges.quote: their light won’t last

edges.reason: Speaks of what rulers as a class stand to win or lose.
edges.quote: What makes rulers last

couplets.gloss: Life under a heartless ruler is like the land in a drought.

edges.reason: Likens a people under a merciless ruler to land left without rain.
edges.quote: a ruler with no tenderness

edges.reason: Asks how the people fare under such a government.
edges.quote: to living beings

edges.reason: Its comparison is aimed at the ruler who withholds his care.
edges.quote: a ruler with no tenderness

edges.reason: The earth with no rain stands for people under a ruler with no tenderness.
edges.quote: What no rain is to the earth

couplets.gloss: Under an unjust ruler, having money is even more painful than having none.

edges.reason: Under a tyrant, owning things hurts more than owning nothing.
edges.quote: having is more painful than having nothing

edges.reason: Lays the misery of rich and poor alike at the tyrant's door.
edges.quote: a ruler who does no justice

couplets.gloss: If a ruler turns away from justice, the rains won't come when they should.

edges.reason: Says the very rains fail once a ruler leaves the path of justice.
edges.quote: acts against justice

edges.reason: Hangs the weather itself on one ruler's conduct.
edges.quote: If the ruler acts against justice

couplets.gloss: If a ruler fails to protect his people, the cows give less milk and even priests forget their scriptures.

edges.reason: Unjust rule dries the cows' milk and drives scripture from memory.
edges.quote: If the protector doesn’t protect

edges.reason: Shows even the learning of those of the six duties lapsing under a bad ruler.
edges.quote: those of the six duties forget their books

edges.reason: Places the blame for this decay on the ruler's failure.
edges.quote: If the protector doesn’t protect

couplets.gloss: A ruler should weigh the offence and punish enough to stop it happening again, but never too much.

edges.reason: Asks that punishment fit the guilt and deter, and never go past that.
edges.quote: punishes to fit it

edges.reason: Lays the duty of measured judgment on the ruler himself.
edges.quote: A ruler is one who looks into a wrong fairly

edges.reason: Tells anyone who disciplines others to weigh the fault and stop at what will correct it.
edges.quote: so that it won’t be done again

couplets.gloss: If you want your power to last, raise the stick high but bring it down gently.

edges.reason: Lasting gains come from raising the blow sharply and letting it land softly.
edges.quote: Raise the blow sharply but let it land softly

edges.reason: The ruler's rod is raised high in warning but must fall soft.
edges.quote: the rod

couplets.gloss: A ruler who terrifies his people with harsh rule ends up with no one on his side and falls fast.

edges.reason: Rule by terror is sure to bring a ruler down, and soon.
edges.quote: lives by what terrifies people

edges.reason: Addressed to the ruler who governs by fear.
edges.quote: A wielder of the cruel sceptre

edges.reason: The cruel sceptre pictures a rule that only hurts.
edges.quote: the cruel sceptre

couplets.gloss: A ruler known among his people for cruelty has a short reign and falls quickly.
keywords: what staff say about the boss

edges.reason: Once his people call him cruel, a ruler's days are numbered.
edges.quote: Our ruler is harsh

edges.reason: Speaks of the ruler whose own people talk of his harshness.
edges.quote: A ruler of whom people say the bitter words

couplets.gloss: A grim ruler nobody can get to see is like a demon sitting on a hoard: his wealth does no one any good.

edges.reason: One who is hard to see holds riches as useless as something a demon has seized.
edges.quote: someone hard to see

edges.reason: His grim face joins his distance in making his wealth a thing to dread.
edges.quote: a sour face

edges.reason: Draws a portrait of the forbidding ruler.
edges.quote: Behold the dour-faced prince

couplets.gloss: However rich a ruler is, being sharp-tongued and unforgiving will bring his wealth to a quick end.

edges.reason: A rough tongue ends even the greatest prosperity quickly.
edges.quote: a harsh tongue

edges.reason: Having no kind eye for others hastens the end of all one has.
edges.quote: no kind eye

edges.reason: Makes the ruler's wealth hang on his manner toward others.
edges.quote: If the prince is harsh of word

couplets.gloss: Cruel words and over-the-top punishments slowly grind away the strength of those in power.

edges.reason: Hard words and heavy penalties wear away the strength they seem to show.
edges.quote: punishment past all measure

edges.reason: Harshness is the file that wears a ruler’s strength thin.
edges.quote: the file that wears away a ruler’s conquering strength

edges.reason: Warns those in charge that over-punishing eats at their own authority.
edges.quote: Harsh words and punishment past all measure

couplets.gloss: A ruler who won't consult his advisers and then loses his temper when things go wrong will see his fortunes shrink.

edges.reason: Raging when his plans fail shrinks a ruler's prosperity.
edges.quote: flies into a rage

edges.reason: Refusing to consult his councillors is where this ruler's trouble starts.
edges.quote: doesn’t think things through with his circle

edges.reason: Describes the ruler who acts alone and then storms at the outcome.
edges.quote: a ruler who doesn’t think things through

couplets.gloss: A ruler who doesn't build his defences in time will panic and fall fast when war suddenly arrives.

edges.reason: Neglected defences turn a sudden war into panic and swift ruin.
edges.quote: doesn’t build defences before war comes

edges.reason: Warns the ruler who has built no defences when war comes.
edges.quote: A ruler who doesn’t build defences

couplets.gloss: The heaviest load the earth has to carry is a harsh government that binds ignorant people to its service.

edges.reason: Calls harsh rule that binds the unlearned to itself the one true weight on the earth.
edges.quote: A harsh sceptre binds the unlearned to itself

edges.reason: Pictures the earth as bearing no burden but this one.
edges.quote: The earth has no burden but that

ideaLinks.reason: A clean mind is said to depend on keeping clean company.
ideaLinks.quote: A pure mind and pure deeds both depend on pure company

ideaLinks.reason: Clean deeds, like a clean mind, rest on the company one keeps.
ideaLinks.quote: pure deeds both depend on pure company

ideaLinks.reason: Virtuous companions bring a man every honour.
ideaLinks.quote: Good company brings every kind of glory

ideaLinks.reason: Giving freely draws one's relatives in close.
ideaLinks.quote: If you can give and speak sweetly, you will be surrounded by kin

ideaLinks.reason: Sweet words gather relatives round a man.
ideaLinks.quote: speak sweetly, you will be surrounded by kin

ideaLinks.reason: Unending fondness among kin brings gains that keep on sprouting.
ideaLinks.quote: many gains that go on sprouting

ideaLinks.reason: Carelessness is said to kill glory.
Daily want is said to kill understanding.
Glory is denied to the careless.
ideaLinks.quote: There is no glory for the careless

ideaLinks.reason: The ruler’s sceptre is named the root of righteousness.
ideaLinks.quote: The ruler’s sceptre stands at the root of the books of the sages and of righteousness

ideaLinks.reason: The books of the sages rest on the sceptre and lapse when the ruler fails at justice.
The rains keep their season only while the ruler keeps to justice.
ideaLinks.quote: Rain and harvest come together in the land of a ruler

ideaLinks.reason: Just rule is what brings rulers renown.
ideaLinks.quote: What makes rulers last is the straight sceptre

ideaLinks.reason: Unjust government darkens a ruler's name.
Sets just rule and unjust government side by side as opposite ways of governing.
ideaLinks.quote: What makes rulers last is the straight sceptre. Without it, their light won’t last

ideaLinks.reason: A ruler who bends the sceptre loses his riches along with his people.
ideaLinks.quote: will lose his riches and his people together

proposals.label: Beasts at Their Hour and Ground
proposals.why: Chapters 49 and 50 argue through animals that win only at their moment or on their ground (crow and owl, ram, stork, crocodile). No image entry covers them, so these couplets carry no USES_IMAGE edge.
